title: Near misses that fail for one reason
statement: Teach and test a word or concept with surface-different examples that share its one deep feature, and near-miss non-examples that each fail for a single reason the feedback names.
example: One vocabulary check shows three surface-different scenes with one shared feature, against three near-miss words that are each wrong for one reason.
detail: A rebuilt lesson's vocabulary check shows three surface-different scenes that share one deep feature, with near-miss words each wrong for exactly one nameable reason, and its feedback names the mismatch; its parameter table says discrimination teaches a concept's edges. The physics misconception card applies the same idea to demonstrations: a law of motion is not to be shown only with stationary examples, but with moving ones too. The point is that the learner has to tell close meanings apart.
